name: GCI_qfingerprint_product_colab (1).ipynb
first_code_snippet: GCI World 2026 - q-fingerprint submission (single file).    python GCI_qfingerprint_submission.py [champion.csv] [weight]
KEY FINDING: every "rate-curve shape" feature (rate_std, rate_range, r24, curvatures...) is a function of ONE number, q = AMT_ANNUITY / AMT_CREDIT.
The real signal is risk as a function of q at FINE resolution (about 800-1500 distinct values = lender loan products), which tree models cannot resolve.
Leak-safe target encodings of q rounded to 3, 4 and 5 decimals (smoothed, nested out-of-fold for training rows) are given to three LightGBM models:
qf_onehot (core features, one-hot categories) | qf_allfam_oh (130 features, one-hot) | qf_mono (core features, monotone EXT_SOURCE constraint).
Held-out (5-fold) AUC: 0.76713 / 0.76678 / 0.76746; their average 0.76843 vs 0.76458 for the previous best recipe.
Final = (1 - W) * champion + W * average of the three models' ranks (W = 0.7; held-out evidence: +0.0040 over the recipe, 5/5 folds positive).
The champion CSV (default: GCI_submission_residual.csv, public 0.76815, made by GCI_solution_final.py + GCI_residual_submission.py) can be replaced by any 61,500-row champion file.
Only train.csv labels and test.csv features are used. No external data, no test labels.
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, lightgbm as lgb
